newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money unchanged, gilt yields steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money unchanged, gilt yields steady.

text.p: Indian call money ended Tuesday in the 9.0-9.25 percent, unchanged from the day's opening levels, dealers said.
Most of the day's trade was in the same range with stray deals at 9.50 percent, they said.
"There are no new market-moving factors to influence call money rates," a dealer at a state-run bank said. "We are awaiting the monetary policy announcement on Saturday."

The Reserve Bank of India announces its monetary policy for the second half of 1996/97 (April-March) on October 19. Bankers expect the central bank to announce a cut in cash reserve requirements, which is expected to improve liquidity and result in a fall in interest rates.
Secondary market prices of government securities were steady in active trade, dealers said.
The volume traded on the National Stock Exchange was 2.13 billion rupees on Tuesday against Monday's 2.45 billion, Kavita Rahalkar, dealer at Birla-Marlin Securities said.
Trade continued to be brisk as banks took trading positions anticipating a fall in interest rates after the monetary policy announcement due on October 19.
"A fall in interest rates will result in an appreciation in the value of investments," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
The 13.5 percent 1997 stock was traded at 12.70 percent on Tuesday unchanged from Monday, dealers said. The 13.50 percent 1998 stock was also unchanged at 13.16 percent.
Commercial paper of top-rated companies were quoted in the 13.0-13.25 percent range, Birla Marlin's Rahalkar said.
Rates on intercorporate deposits remained steady in the 18-20 percent range, dealers said.
